---
title: "Weekly Trends of Multiple Virus Cases and Their RPKMF in Different Districts"
output:
  pdf_document: default
  html_notebook: default
---

```{r}
# Load necessary packages
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
library(dplyr)
library(zoo)
library(ggpubr)
library(patchwork)
library(lubridate)
library(tidyquant)
library(rprojroot)
library(stringr)
library(eoffice)  # For generating PPTX files

# Set file paths
case_data_table <- sprintf("%s/data/IAV_RoV_NoV_case_year_week_data.tsv", find_rstudio_root_file())
rpkmf_data_table <- sprintf("%s/data/IAV_RoV_NoV_RPKMF_data.tsv", find_rstudio_root_file())

# Read data
case_data <- fread(case_data_table, sep = "\t", header = TRUE)
rpkmf_data <- fread(rpkmf_data_table, sep = "\t", header = TRUE)

# Define viruses to analyze
viruses <- list(
  list(name = "IAV", fullname = "Influenza A Virus"),
  list(name = "RoV", fullname = "Rotavirus"),
  list(name = "NoV", fullname = "Norovirus")
)

# Set统一颜色 for all viruses
colors <- c("Cases" = "#d62728", "RPKMF" = "#00A087")

# Convert date format
convert_date <- function(date_str) {
  result <- as.Date(date_str, format = "%Y/%m/%d")
  if (any(is.na(result))) {
    result <- as.Date(date_str, format = "%Y-%m-%d")
  }
  return(result)
}

# Process RPKMF data: convert date and extract year and week
rpkmf_data <- rpkmf_data %>%
  mutate(Date = convert_date(Date),
         year = year(Date),
         week = week(Date)) %>%
  rename(District = District)

# Identify unique districts present in the data
target_districts <- unique(case_data$District)
print(paste("Analyzing data for districts:", paste(target_districts, collapse = ", ")))

# Filter data for the target districts
case_data <- case_data %>% filter(District %in% target_districts)
rpkmf_data <- rpkmf_data %>% filter(District %in% target_districts)

# Aggregate RPKMF data by week and district (calculate mean RPKMF per week)
processed_rpkmf_data <- rpkmf_data %>%
  group_by(year, week, District) %>%
  summarise(
    IAV_RPKMF = mean(IAV_RPKMF, na.rm = TRUE),
    RoV_RPKMF = mean(RoV_RPKMF, na.rm = TRUE),
    NoV_RPKMF = mean(NoV_RPKMF, na.rm = TRUE),
    Date = max(Date)
  ) %>%  # Use the latest date in the week for plotting
  ungroup()

# Merge RPKMF data with case data
merged_data <- left_join(processed_rpkmf_data, case_data, by = c("year", "week", "District"))

# Create date labels (Year-WWeek)
merged_data <- merged_data %>%
  mutate(date_label = paste0(year, "-W", str_pad(week, width = 2, side = "left", pad = "0")))

# Create overall aggregated data: sum of cases and mean of RPKMF across all districts
overall_data <- merged_data %>%
  group_by(year, week, Date, date_label) %>%
  summarise(
    IAV_cases = sum(IAV_cases, na.rm = TRUE),
    RoV_cases = sum(RoV_cases, na.rm = TRUE),
    NoV_cases = sum(NoV_cases, na.rm = TRUE),
    IAV_RPKMF = mean(IAV_RPKMF, na.rm = TRUE),
    RoV_RPKMF = mean(RoV_RPKMF, na.rm = TRUE),
    NoV_RPKMF = mean(NoV_RPKMF, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Create correlation plot function for RPKMF vs Cases for a specific virus
create_correlation_plot <- function(data, virus) {
  # Extract virus-specific columns
  x_col <- paste0(virus$name, "_RPKMF")
  y_col <- paste0(virus$name, "_cases")
  
  # Filter out rows with missing values
  plot_data <- data %>% select(all_of(c(x_col, y_col))) %>% na.omit()
  
  p_cor <- ggscatter(plot_data, x = x_col, y = y_col, 
                     add = "reg.line", conf.int = TRUE, 
                     cor.coef = TRUE, cor.method = "pearson", 
                     cor.coef.size = 5, color = colors["RPKMF"], 
                     xlab = paste0(virus$fullname, " RPKMF"), 
                     ylab = paste0("Weekly ", virus$fullname, " Cases")) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
      axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "none"
    )
  return(p_cor)
}

# Create trend plot function for a specific virus in a district or overall
create_trend_plot <- function(data, virus, title, is_overall = FALSE) {
  # Extract virus-specific columns
  rpkfm_col <- paste0(virus$name, "_RPKMF")
  cases_col <- paste0(virus$name, "_cases")
  
  # Calculate scaling factors for visual balance
  max_cases <- max(data[[cases_col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  max_rpkfm <- max(data[[rpkfm_col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Handle case where max_rpkfm might be zero to avoid division by zero
  if (max_rpkfm == 0) {
    scaling_factor_rpkfm <- 1
  } else {
    scaling_factor_rpkfm <- max_cases / max_rpkfm * 0.8
  }
  
  # Create trend plot with both metrics
  p_trend <- ggplot(data, aes(x = as.Date(Date))) +
    # Cases - primary y-axis
    geom_point(aes(y = .data[[cases_col]], color = "Cases"), alpha = 0.6, size = 2) +
    geom_ma(aes(y = .data[[cases_col]], color = "Cases"), ma_fun = SMA, n = 3, linetype = "solid", size = 1.2) +
    
    # RPKMF - secondary y-axis
    geom_point(aes(y = .data[[rpkfm_col]] * scaling_factor_rpkfm, color = "RPKMF"), alpha = 0.6, size = 2) +
    geom_ma(aes(y = .data[[rpkfm_col]] * scaling_factor_rpkfm, color = "RPKMF"), ma_fun = SMA, n = 3, linetype = "solid", size = 1.2) +
    
    # Set统一颜色
    scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
    
    # Configure primary and secondary y-axes
    scale_y_continuous(
      name = ifelse(is_overall, 
                   paste0("Total Weekly ", virus$fullname, " Cases (All Districts)"), 
                   paste0("Weekly ", virus$fullname, " Cases")),
      sec.axis = sec_axis(
        ~ . / scaling_factor_rpkfm,
        name = ifelse(is_overall, 
                   paste0("Average ", virus$fullname, " RPKMF (All Districts)"), 
                   paste0(virus$fullname, " RPKMF"))
      )
    ) +
    
    # Configure x-axis date format and breaks
    scale_x_date(
      labels = function(x) {
        year <- year(x)
        week <- week(x)
        paste0(year, "-W", str_pad(week, width = 2, side = "left", pad = "0"))
      },
      date_breaks = "4 weeks"
    ) +
    
    # Set theme and labels
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    labs(color = "Metric") +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 0.5, size = 12),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
      legend.position = ifelse(is_overall, "right", "bottom"),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold")
    ) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      x = "Year-Week",
      color = "Metric"
    )
  
  return(p_trend)
}

# Wrapper function for district trend plots
create_district_trend_plot <- function(district_data, district, virus) {
  create_trend_plot(district_data, virus, paste(virus$fullname, "in", district, "District"), is_overall = FALSE)
}

# Create combined plots for all districts for a specific virus
create_combined_district_plots <- function(all_data, virus) {
  # Split data by district
  district_data_list <- split(all_data, all_data$District)
  
  # Generate a list of plots for each district
  plot_list <- lapply(target_districts, function(district) {
    district_data <- district_data_list[[district]]
    p_trend <- create_district_trend_plot(district_data, district, virus) + 
      theme(legend.position = "none")  # Remove legend from individual plots
    return(p_trend)
  })
  
  # Combine all plots into a single grid
  combined_plots <- wrap_plots(plot_list, ncol = 2) +
    plot_annotation(
      title = paste(virus$fullname, "Cases vs RPKMF Across Districts"),
      theme = theme(
        plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
      )
    )
  
  # Extract legend from one of the plots
  legend_plot <- create_district_trend_plot(district_data_list[[target_districts[1]]], target_districts[1], virus) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  legend <- get_legend(legend_plot)
  
  # Combine plots with legend
  final_plot <- combined_plots / legend + plot_layout(heights = c(10, 1))
  
  return(final_plot)
}

# Create combined correlation plots for all districts for a specific virus
create_combined_correlation_plots <- function(all_data, virus) {
  # Split data by district
  district_data_list <- split(all_data, all_data$District)
  
  # Generate a list of correlation plots for each district
  plot_list <- lapply(target_districts, function(district) {
    district_data <- district_data_list[[district]]
    p_cor <- create_correlation_plot(district_data, virus) +
      ggtitle(paste(district, "District")) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"))
    return(p_cor)
  })
  
  # Determine layout based on number of districts
  cols <- ifelse(length(target_districts) > 2, 2, length(target_districts))
  
  # Combine all correlation plots into a single plot
  combined_correlation_plots <- wrap_plots(plot_list, ncol = cols) +
    plot_annotation(
      title = paste("Correlation Between", virus$fullname, "RPKMF and Weekly Cases Across Districts"),
      theme = theme(
        plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
      )
    )
  
  return(combined_correlation_plots)
}

# Create output directory if it doesn't exist
chart_dir <- sprintf("%s/charts", find_rstudio_root_file())
if (!dir.exists(chart_dir)) {
  dir.create(chart_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

# Generate plots for each district and each virus
for (virus in viruses) {
  for (district in target_districts) {
    district_data <- merged_data %>% filter(District == district)
    
    # Skip if no data for this district
    if (nrow(district_data) == 0) {
      warning(paste("No data available for", district, "District and", virus$fullname))
      next
    }
    
    # Create trend plot
    p_trend <- create_district_trend_plot(district_data, district, virus) +
      theme(legend.position = "right")
    
    # Create correlation scatter plot
    p_cor <- create_correlation_plot(district_data, virus)
    
    # Define common filenames for PDF and PPTX
    base_filename_trend <- sprintf("%s/%s_%s_flu_trend", chart_dir, district, virus$name)
    base_filename_cor <- sprintf("%s/%s_%s_rpkmf_correlation", chart_dir, district, virus$name)
    
    # Save as PDF
    ggsave(sprintf("%s.pdf", base_filename_trend), p_trend, width = 14, height = 9)
    ggsave(sprintf("%s.pdf", base_filename_cor), p_cor, width = 10, height = 8)
    
    # Save as PPTX with consistent filenames
    topptx(p_trend, filename = sprintf("%s.pptx", base_filename_trend), height = 9, width = 14)
    topptx(p_cor, filename = sprintf("%s.pptx", base_filename_cor), height = 8, width = 10)
  }
  
  # Generate overall plots (aggregated across all districts) for this virus
  # Create overall trend plot
  p_overall_trend <- create_trend_plot(
    overall_data, 
    virus, 
    paste("Overall", virus$fullname, "Cases vs Average RPKMF (Three Districts Combined)"), 
    is_overall = TRUE
  )
  
  # Create overall correlation plot
  p_overall_cor <- create_correlation_plot(overall_data, virus) +
    ggtitle(paste("Overall Correlation for", virus$fullname, "(Three Districts Combined)")) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"))
  
  # Define filenames for overall plots
  base_filename_overall_trend <- sprintf("%s/overall_%s_trend", chart_dir, virus$name)
  base_filename_overall_cor <- sprintf("%s/overall_%s_rpkmf_correlation", chart_dir, virus$name)
  
  # Save overall plots as PDF
  ggsave(sprintf("%s.pdf", base_filename_overall_trend), p_overall_trend, width = 14, height = 9)
  ggsave(sprintf("%s.pdf", base_filename_overall_cor), p_overall_cor, width = 10, height = 8)
  
  # Save overall plots as PPTX
  topptx(p_overall_trend, filename = sprintf("%s.pptx", base_filename_overall_trend), height = 9, width = 14)
  topptx(p_overall_cor, filename = sprintf("%s.pptx", base_filename_overall_cor), height = 8, width = 10)
  
  # Create and save multi-district trend plot for this virus
  p_multi_district <- create_combined_district_plots(merged_data, virus)
  base_filename_multi <- sprintf("%s/all_districts_%s_trend_comparison", chart_dir, virus$name)
  ggsave(sprintf("%s.pdf", base_filename_multi), p_multi_district, width = 20, height = 12)
  topptx(p_multi_district, filename = sprintf("%s.pptx", base_filename_multi), height = 12, width = 20)
  
  # Create and save combined correlation plots for this virus
  p_combined_correlation <- create_combined_correlation_plots(merged_data, virus)
  base_filename_correlation <- sprintf("%s/all_districts_%s_correlation_comparison", chart_dir, virus$name)
  ggsave(sprintf("%s.pdf", base_filename_correlation), p_combined_correlation, width = 20, height = 16)
  topptx(p_combined_correlation, filename = sprintf("%s.pptx", base_filename_correlation), height = 16, width = 20)
}

```
